stories.title: HP launches OmniBook 5 AI PC for students
stories.summary: HP has introduced the OmniBook 5 AI PC, featuring an Intel Core 5 320 processor and a 14-inch OLED display. The company says the laptop is built for students managing coursework and career demands. It includes a battery rated for up to 42 hours of local video playback.

stories.title: Detroit students face gap between career talk and experience
stories.summary: A survey of 83 young Detroiters found that while 78 percent had heard from guest speakers or mentors, fewer than half had completed paid work experience. Just 35 percent received hands-on training. The city's teenagers are not short on talk about work. They are short on work.

stories.title: How to develop a teaching-focused career at Canadian post-secondary institutions - University Affairs
Sam Heughan funds scholarships at former drama school
stories.summary: Actor Sam Heughan is funding three annual scholarships for undergraduate students at the Royal Conservatoire of Scotland. He has also launched the Write Start creative commission to provide financial support for emerging artists. The contribution extends beyond tuition assistance to help students gain access to the industry.

stories.title: GLOBIS University expands in India to attract MBA students
stories.summary: Japanese business school GLOBIS University has opened a hub in Gurugram to recruit Indian MBA aspirants. The university currently has 12 Indian students enrolled in its full-time programme in Japan. It aims to expand corporate training for Japanese companies operating in the region.

stories.title: Top 10 Affordable Student Cities in UK for International Students 2027 - Shiksha.com
Indian students going to foreign nations are more discerning now | Hindustan Times Lucknow - newspaper - Magzter
International student interest shifts from US and UK to Asia
stories.summary: A survey of 437 universities found that international undergraduate enrollment in the UK fell 19 percent between October and August compared to the previous year. The US recorded a 13 percent decline. Tighter visa and immigration policies are prompting students to consider universities in Asia and Europe.

stories.title: Philadelphia struggles to retain international graduates
stories.summary: Research from the Economic League of Greater Philadelphia shows that of 1,333 international graduates working on optional practical training in 2023, only 421 stayed in the region. The city hosts approximately 23,000 international students annually, but few remain to work in the area after graduation.

stories.title: IPS officer Sharan Kamble shares path from manual labour to service
stories.summary: Sharan Kamble has been appointed as an IPS officer after a career path that included selling vegetables and manual labour. He often studied by lantern light while living in a home without electricity. His journey is cited as an example of overcoming financial challenges to pursue education.

stories.title: Government employees weigh pay commission hike options
stories.summary: Central government employees are debating the impact of a higher fitment factor versus a higher annual increment rate under the 8th Pay Commission. Current 7th Pay Commission terms provide a 2.57 fitment factor and a 3 percent annual increment. Employee associations are now requesting higher figures.

stories.title: Kolkata school team wins national chess title
stories.summary: A team from Bhavan's Gangabux Kanoria Vidyamandir in Kolkata won the boys' championship at the CBSE National Chess Championship in Jalandhar. The tournament, held from October 14 to 18, featured teams from schools across India and abroad. This marks the team's second consecutive win.

stories.title: Rawal and Patil deliver strong performances in T20 Trophy
stories.summary: Pratika Rawal scored 86 runs off 52 balls to lead Railways to victory over Mumbai in the Senior Women's T20 Trophy. Meanwhile, Shreyanka Patil took three wickets against Baroda. Both players are currently competing in the Super Eight stage of the tournament in Ahmedabad.

stories.title: Mohit Ulva joins Saurashtra squad after Asia Cup performance
stories.summary: Eighteen-year-old Mohit Ulva has been added to Saurashtra's Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy squad. The call-up follows his unbeaten 49-run performance in the Under-19 Asia Cup final against Pakistan. The Saurashtra Cricket Association confirmed his inclusion for the upcoming matches in Indore.

stories.title: Karachi Kings social media post backfires after Asia Cup final
stories.summary: The Karachi Kings franchise faced criticism on social media after mocking the Indian Under-19 team before the Asia Cup final. The post followed Pakistan's one-wicket defeat to India. The franchise's attempt to taunt the opposition resulted in significant negative feedback after the match concluded.

stories.title: Disha Kasat sets Indian record for sixes in T20 match
stories.summary: Vidarbha batter Disha Kasat hit 10 sixes in a single innings during a Senior Women's T20 Trophy match against Delhi. She is the first Indian woman to reach this total in a T20 match, surpassing the previous record of nine. Her 91 not out secured an eight-wicket win.

stories.title: Prime Minister Modi praises India U19 cricket team
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated the Indian Under-19 team following their one-wicket victory over Pakistan in the Asia Cup final. He described the win as a proud moment for Indian cricket and stated that the performance would serve as an inspiration for other young athletes.

stories.title: Mohit Ulva keeps it simple in U19 Asia Cup final
stories.summary: India secured their ninth U19 Asia Cup title after a one-wicket victory over Pakistan. Mohit Ulva, a specialist bowler, scored an unbeaten 49 off 26 balls to seal the chase. The youngster says he kept things simple under pressure. The ball was hit accordingly.

stories.title: Pakistan captain gracious after U19 Asia Cup loss
stories.summary: Pakistan captain Farhan Yousuf praised India after his team lost the U19 Asia Cup final by one wicket. India successfully chased a target of 338 on the final ball of the match. The defeat was described as hard to take by the losing side.

stories.title: Virender Sehwag praises India's U19 Asia Cup win
stories.summary: India ended a five-year title drought by chasing 338 to beat Pakistan in the U19 Asia Cup final. Mohit Ulva scored an unbeaten 49 off 26 balls to secure the one-wicket win. Virender Sehwag expressed his approval of the performance.

stories.title: Mohit Ulva scripts last-ball win in U19 Asia Cup
stories.summary: India defeated Pakistan by one wicket to win the U19 Asia Cup 2026. Mohit Ulva, an 18-year-old from Jamnagar, entered the crease at number 10 and scored an unbeaten 49 off 26 balls. The match was decided on the final delivery.

stories.title: India celebrates U19 Asia Cup victory over Pakistan
stories.summary: India beat Pakistan by one wicket to win the U19 Asia Cup in Al Amerat. The Indian team engaged in animated celebrations following the final-ball victory. The match featured a target of 338 and a late-order contribution from Mohit Ulva.

stories.title: India wins U19 Asia Cup with last-ball boundary
stories.summary: India defeated Pakistan by one wicket to lift the U19 Asia Cup. Needing eight runs in the final over, number 10 batter Mohit Ulva scored an unbeaten 49 off 26 balls. The winning runs were secured with a boundary off the final delivery.

stories.title: Iranian students win gold at astronomy competition
stories.summary: A six-member Iranian team secured gold medals at the Open World Astronomy Olympiad in Russia. The competition, held from November 6 to 14, involved students aged 14 to 18. Participants competed in theoretical, practical, observational, and test rounds conducted entirely in English.

stories.title: Iranian team secures six golds at astronomy event
stories.summary: Six Iranian students won gold medals at the fifth Open World Astronomy Olympiad held in Russia. The competition, which ran from November 6 to 14, is described as a modern and rapidly growing event. The students were recognized for their dedication and academic excellence.

stories.title: Iranian students win six gold medals at Russia 2026 Open World Astronomy Olympiad - www.taghribnews.com
IOAA-Jr 2026: India Wins Five Medals at International Junior Astronomy and Astrophysics Olympiad! - Telegraph India
Iran takes six gold medals in astronomy olympiad
stories.summary: The Iranian national B team won six gold medals at the Open World Astronomy Olympiad 2026 in Russia. The competition took place from November 6 to 14 in the Sirius Federal Territory. All six team members received gold medals for their performance.

stories.title: Modi opens LED dome planetarium in Mysuru
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the COSMOS Planetarium in Mysuru, India's first LED dome facility. Modi stated the planetarium would inspire young minds to explore the universe and develop scientific curiosity. The project is intended to contribute to the nation's scientific journey.

stories.title: Ancient DNA links Peru infant to trisomy 13
stories.summary: Researchers identified a 1,600-year-old infant with cyclopia at a Nasca cemetery in Peru. DNA analysis published in PNAS linked the condition to trisomy 13, a chromosomal abnormality. The study combined skeletal and archaeological evidence to confirm the diagnosis of the rare developmental condition.

stories.title: Guide lists life skills for children before high school
stories.summary: A new resource suggests children should master 10 life skills before entering high school, including managing money and responding to emergencies. While schools focus on academic examinations, the guide notes that many students reach adolescence without preparation for these everyday responsibilities.

stories.title: Harvard releases AI guidance matrix for students
stories.summary: The Harvard Graduate School of Education has launched an AI Guidance by Age Matrix to assist parents and teachers. The resource draws on over 5,000 research publications to examine how artificial intelligence affects learning at different stages of human development.

stories.title: CBSE releases Class 12 English sample paper
stories.summary: The Central Board of Secondary Education has published the English Core sample question paper for the 2026-27 academic session. The document outlines the examination structure, question types, and marking scheme. Students can download the paper to prepare for the upcoming board examinations.

stories.title: CBSE offers practice questions for Class 10 English
stories.summary: The Central Board of Secondary Education has provided 50 multiple-choice questions for the 2027 Class 10 English pre-board exams. The materials cover reading, grammar, and literature. Students are encouraged to use these questions to improve their performance in the upcoming board examinations.

stories.title: CBSE publishes Class 12 Physical Education sample paper
stories.summary: The Central Board of Secondary Education has released the Physical Education sample paper for the 2026-27 academic session. The 70-mark theory paper includes 37 questions across five sections. Students can access the marking scheme and exam pattern on the official academic website.

stories.title: A-Levels to Everything You Need to Know in 2026 - HR News
Assam Police releases admit cards for ASI recruitment
stories.summary: The State Level Police Recruitment Board in Assam has released admit cards for Assistant Sub-Inspector candidates. Applicants must use their login credentials on the official websites to access the documents required for the written examination. The cards contain essential information for the upcoming recruitment process.

stories.title: Teaching kids to think for themselves in the age of AI - The Economist
Physics Wallah offers 27 percent discount on IOQM batch
stories.summary: Physics Wallah is offering a 27 percent discount on its IOQM 2027 batch for a limited period. The price has been reduced to 2,999 rupees from the original 4,116 rupees. The company describes the move as an opportunity for aspirants to access structured mathematics preparation.

stories.title: Falkner High students discuss AI in utility careers
stories.summary: Falkner High School students recently met with representatives from the Central Service Association to discuss the role of technology in utility industries. The visitors covered automation and new tools currently reshaping the workplace. The school noted the session provided a look at how artificial intelligence affects utility careers.

stories.title: Fontana Unified robotics teams head to World Robot Olympiad
stories.summary: Fifteen students from the Fontana Unified School District will compete at the World Robot Olympiad in Puerto Rico this December. Six teams qualified for the international event by designing and programming robots to solve problems. The competition includes participants ranging from 8 to 22 years old.

stories.title: Turkmenistan students win medals at mathematics Olympiad
stories.summary: Students from Turkmenistan secured one gold and two bronze medals at the International Team Mathematics Olympiad in Poland. Oguzhan Garlyev took first place in the individual competition. The event hosted university students from several nations, including the United Kingdom, Austria, and the Republic of Poland.

stories.title: Tribal Affairs Ministry opens scholarship applications
stories.summary: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs has invited applications for its 2026-27 scholarship scheme for Scheduled Tribe students. The program provides tuition fee support and an annual stipend of 36,000 rupees. Eligible students pursuing undergraduate or postgraduate courses at selected institutions may apply until November 30.

stories.title: UGC opens applications for Ishan Uday scholarship
stories.summary: The University Grants Commission is accepting applications for the Ishan Uday scholarship, which provides 80,000 rupees annually to students from India's eight North Eastern states. The scheme supports approximately 10,000 students pursuing undergraduate degrees. Applications for the 2026-27 academic year close on November 30.

stories.title: Dr. Sergio Sokol scholarship opens for medical students
stories.summary: The Dr. Sergio Sokol Scholarship for Future Doctors has opened its 2026-2027 application cycle. The program offers a one-time 1,000 dollar award to undergraduate, graduate, and medical students. The scholarship seeks candidates who demonstrate academic commitment and a passion for serving others through healthcare.

stories.title: Green Institute fellowship opens for sustainability leaders
stories.summary: The Green Institute is accepting applications for its 2026-2027 global fellowship for sustainability advocates aged 18 to 35. Participants will develop climate advocacy skills and compete for a 1,000 dollar post-fellowship award. The program aims to establish school-based environmental clubs. Applications close on January 7, 2027.

stories.title: Morris Animal Foundation offers veterinary research stipends
stories.summary: The Morris Animal Foundation is inviting applications for its 2026 Veterinary Student Scholar Program. The competitive initiative provides a 5,500 dollar stipend for students to conduct mentored research on the health of dogs, cats, equids, and wildlife. The foundation funds studies in clinical, laboratory, and field settings.

stories.title: British Council honours 64 outstanding students at Scholars’ Award - Daily Sun
Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam society announces scholarship exam
stories.summary: The Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Welfare Society has launched the Bright Student Award Scholarship Exam for students in classes 4 to 12. The initiative offers cash prizes up to 1 lakh rupees, along with medals and laptops. The exam is designed to identify and reward academic potential.

stories.title: Last date for submission of applications under the National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme for academic year 2026-27
Tripura launches Navgati scholarship for students
stories.summary: The Tripura government has launched the Navgati Scholarship Programme to support 1,000 meritorious students from economically disadvantaged families. Funded by Shriram Finance Limited as a corporate social responsibility initiative, the program aims to ensure financial hardship does not prevent students from continuing their education.

stories.title: ProTeen announces scholarship for career guidance
stories.summary: ProTeen has opened applications for its Young Achievers Scholarship, offering a cumulative 10 lakh rupees to 40 students across India. The program evaluates career potential rather than academic marks. Students in classes 10 and 12 must submit an essay and complete an interest assessment by November 30.

stories.title: GraceKennedy Foundation awards over $31m in scholarships
stories.summary: The GraceKennedy Foundation has awarded over $31 million in scholarships to 90 Jamaican tertiary students for the 2026/27 academic year. The foundation says the initiative reinforces its commitment to nurturing the next generation of leaders. The awards were presented under the theme, Where Potential Blooms.

stories.title: Private school invites 2000 students for scholarship programme
stories.summary: Abraham Seed Private School International has invited 2000 students to compete for its 2026/27 scholarship programme. The school director stated that 200 students will be selected following tests in Mathematics, English and general subjects. The school describes the initiative as part of its decade-long corporate social responsibility programme.

stories.title: 77 per cent of foreign medical graduates fail October exam
stories.summary: Results for the October 2026 Foreign Medical Graduate Examination show that 77 percent of candidates failed to secure minimum qualifying marks. Out of the total participants, 9,354 candidates qualified to pursue medical registration in India, while 31,539 failed. The results highlight challenges for students pursuing MBBS degrees abroad.

stories.title: PMK calls for NEET review after low admission rates
stories.summary: PMK president Anbumani Ramadoss has demanded an urgent review of the NEET entrance test. Official data shows that only five percent of government school students admitted under Tamil Nadu's 7.5 percent reservation quota cleared the exam on their first attempt. The party questions if the test meets its objectives.

stories.title: Rajasthan board postpones February 2027 exams
stories.summary: The Rajasthan Board of Secondary Education has postponed its Class 10 and 12 examinations originally scheduled for February 2027. The board cited the upcoming Census as the reason for the delay. Revised dates have not yet been announced for the affected students.

stories.title: Bar Council of India to release AIBE 22 admit cards
stories.summary: The Bar Council of India is set to release admit cards for the All India Bar Examination 22 today. Registered candidates must download their hall tickets from the official website to gain entry to the November 29 examination. The council has not specified a release time.

stories.title: Students with Type-1 diabetes granted extra exam time
stories.summary: Students with Type-1 diabetes will receive 20 minutes of extra time per hour during the KEAM entrance examination. The Higher Education Minister stated the decision follows a medical certificate requirement. The policy was approved after representations from the Type One Diabetes Foundation regarding potential blood sugar fluctuations.

stories.title: Karnataka Examinations Authority releases KCET 2027 syllabus
stories.summary: The Karnataka Examinations Authority has published the subject-wise syllabus for the 2027 Undergraduate Common Entrance Test. The documents cover Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics and Biology topics from the first and second PUC classes. Candidates can download the PDFs from the official website to begin their preparation.

stories.title: IIT Delhi sets JEE Advanced 2027 date for May 23
stories.summary: IIT Delhi has scheduled the JEE Advanced 2027 examination for May 23. Candidates must rank among the top 2.5 lakh students in the JEE Main 2027 to be eligible. The institute has launched an official website to outline the criteria for prospective applicants.

stories.title: Parents urge CBSE to adjust Class X exam schedule
stories.summary: Parents in Assam have requested that the CBSE review its 2027 Class X examination schedule. The current timetable places English and Assamese language papers on consecutive days. Parents warn that the lack of revision time between major exams could place unnecessary pressure on students.

stories.title: NTA clarifies category selection for JEE Main 2027
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency has issued guidance on category selection for JEE Main 2027 applicants. Indian nationals and NRIs with Aadhaar cards must select the Indian Nationals category, while foreign citizens and OCI cardholders are directed to the Foreign Nationals category. Specific instructions apply to NRIs without Aadhaar.

stories.title: IIT Delhi confirms JEE Advanced 2027 details
stories.summary: IIT Delhi will conduct the JEE Advanced 2027 examination on May 23. The exam allows for the use of an on-screen basic non-scientific calculator. Candidates are permitted a maximum of two attempts in consecutive years, starting from the year they pass their Class 12 examinations.

stories.title: Uttarakhand board releases UTET 2026 results
stories.summary: The Uttarakhand Board of School Education has released the results for the 2026 Teacher Eligibility Test. Candidates can download their scorecards and marksheet from the official portal until November 25. Access requires a registration number, password and the completion of a captcha verification.

stories.title: Canberra aims to increase Southeast Asian student intake
stories.summary: The ACT Government has announced an ambition to attract 30 percent more students from Southeast Asia by 2030. Chief Minister Andrew Barr stated the goal aims to add 400 students to the current 1350. The plan arrives as the Federal Government seeks to control international student growth.

stories.title: UK student visa applications drop 20 per cent
stories.summary: Home Office figures reveal a 20 percent decline in international student visa applications over the past year. The statistics show 349,900 main applicants for the period. The drop follows tighter immigration rules and increased visa refusals, raising concerns over the UK's appeal as a study destination.

stories.title: Malta chamber warns against foreign student fee hikes
stories.summary: The Malta Chamber of SMEs has requested urgent talks with the government regarding proposed fee increases for non-EU students. The chamber warns that higher costs could undermine Malta's competitiveness as an education hub and divert prospective students to competing countries, impacting the wider economy.

stories.title: Canada freezes intake cap for international students till 2029 in new immigration plan - The Indian Express

stories.title: Governments tighten study visa scrutiny
stories.summary: Governments are increasing compliance checks as study visa issuance hits lows in Canada and the US. Agencies are training officers to identify applicants using false pretences, while the UK faces a spike in refusals. The process of proving one is a genuine student has become more involved.

stories.title: Australia narrows family visa eligibility for graduates
stories.summary: From 13 November 2026, the Department of Home Affairs will restrict which family members can join international graduates on a Temporary Graduate visa. Applicants can now only include partners or children who already held a dependent visa on their previous student or graduate permit.

UK Business Schools See 18% Drop In Overseas Enrolments Following Visa Changes - NDTV Profit
Canada sets international student targets through 2029
stories.summary: Canada plans to welcome 150,000 new international students annually from 2027 to 2029. The targets are part of a broader immigration plan to manage temporary resident arrivals while addressing labour market needs. The government aims to balance these arrivals alongside 220,000 temporary workers each year.

stories.title: India defends visa sovereignty following speaker denials
stories.summary: The Ministry of External Affairs stated that visa decisions are a sovereign matter after 115 foreign speakers were denied entry to the Bharat Summit. MP Shashi Tharoor had criticised the government for blocking the guests, who were invited to discuss global affairs and electoral integrity.

stories.title: Korean regions face post-graduation labor hurdles
stories.summary: International students are filling labor gaps in Korea's shrinking regions, yet only 34.3 percent of graduates who remain in the country secure employment. Experts suggest that current policies are failing to help these graduates put down roots in the communities where they studied.

stories.title: UK student visa applications drop 31 percent
stories.summary: UK student visa applications fell by 31 percent in October compared to the same period last year. Industry observers attribute the decline to shifting university recruitment strategies, rising living costs and recent changes to post-study work rights for international students.

stories.title: Karnataka introduces AI to government high schools
stories.summary: The Karnataka Department of School Education and Literacy is adding AI to the Class 9 curriculum for 1,800 government schools. Guest teachers will instruct students on Python, computer vision and generative AI under the National Skills Qualifications Framework. The curriculum aims to provide foundational technical skills.

stories.title: California teachers union seeks generative AI moratorium
stories.summary: A teachers union has requested a three-year halt on student-facing generative AI in California classrooms, citing a need for stronger protections. While Los Angeles Unified already restricts AI on district devices, the debate continues over how to safely integrate the technology into the learning environment.

stories.title: UT students use AI to develop financial technology in inaugural FinTech at Rocky Top competition - WBIR
Professors urge CSU system to use AI for admin work instead of instruction - Sacramento Bee
UPDATE: California teachers union calls for 3-year pause on AI in K-8 classrooms - EdSource
Stanford study questions AI utility in classrooms
stories.summary: A review of 52 studies by Stanford University's AI Hub for Education suggests that most AI tools do not improve student learning. The report concludes that education-specific chatbots are not necessarily superior to general tools and that time-saving features for teachers may have unintended consequences for students.

stories.title: AI is in Bibb classrooms, ‘not going away.’ The rules depend on the assignment - Macon Telegraph
Stanford adds paper-based testing to curb AI use
stories.summary: Stanford University is introducing in-class reading quizzes and handwritten essays for freshmen to combat AI-assisted cheating. The changes to required courses aim to ensure that grades reflect a student's own knowledge. The university is shifting back to paper-based activities to verify what students have learned.

stories.title: UWT courses explore the societal impact of AI
stories.summary: Professor Ellen Moore is teaching two courses at UW Tacoma focused on the influence of artificial intelligence on media, culture and power. The classes aim to educate students on how AI affects the world rather than focusing on how to use the technology for personal tasks.

stories.title: Odisha launches robotic labs in government schools
stories.summary: Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi has inaugurated robotic laboratories in 807 government schools at a cost of Rs 164.33 crore. The state also launched the Nipun App to support foundational learning for primary students. The initiative marks a push toward technology-based practical education.

stories.title: AI training and clear policies went with teacher confidence but not cheating worries, CWU survey finds
stories.summary: A Central Washington University survey of 222 high school teachers found that clear AI policies and training correlated with higher teacher confidence. The study noted no link between these initiatives and teacher morale or concerns regarding student cheating. Districts are advised to focus on classroom practice and assignment design.

stories.title: Headteachers must prioritise early literacy and numeracy to improve learning
stories.summary: Foundational literacy and numeracy are essential for the success of any education system, according to recent guidance. Schools are urged to verify that children can read and write independently before focusing on examination results or infrastructure. These skills remain the core of the lower primary curriculum.

stories.title: Beyond the classroom: Diverse career opportunities available to Kenyan teachers
stories.summary: Teaching remains the foundation of the profession, but educators possess skills applicable to leadership, research, policy formulation, and administration. Professional fulfilment for many teachers extends beyond the classroom, allowing them to influence education at institutional, county, and national levels. The career path is not limited to traditional instruction.

stories.title: Why corporal punishment persists in Indian classrooms
stories.summary: A Class 9 student in Chennai stopped attending school after experiencing physical abuse from a teacher. The teacher reportedly threatened to fail the student when the mother attempted to complain. The practice ceased only after parents threatened to involve the police. The student's name has been changed.

stories.title: The silent cost of India’s research boom on classrooms
stories.summary: UGC norms require assistant professors to teach at least 16 hours weekly, a mandate that may not apply to private institutions. Experts suggest that forcing faculty to balance research and teaching simultaneously is impacting research integrity and classroom quality. The strain is becoming visible in aggregated data.

stories.title: Experts who study AI in classrooms ranked what matters most, and it isn’t the technology
stories.summary: Seventy specialists from 18 countries ranked basic AI literacy as the most critical trend for the next three years. While many conversations focus on AI tutors or automated grading tools, experts argue that teaching students and teachers how these systems function remains the top priority for education.

stories.title: Are schools equipping students for higher education or merely training them to ace exams?
stories.summary: A professor noted that students who scored over 90 percent in secondary exams struggled with basic accounting tasks. The issue was attributed to a focus on memorising theory rather than developing practical competence. Higher education assumes skills that were never encouraged during the students' time in school.

stories.title: How can vice principals adapt to curriculum changes and educational technology?
stories.summary: Vice principals are tasked with helping staff navigate new curriculum policies and digital tools. The role requires supporting professional development and encouraging the effective use of technology. Success depends on continuous learning, clear communication, and proper planning to ensure students receive relevant skills in an evolving educational landscape.

stories.title: Building a team of educators that meets the requirements of educational development in the new era
stories.summary: The Ninh Binh Education Department is implementing solutions to address human resource challenges and improve management capacity. Director Nguyen Tien Dung stated that the teaching staff remains the decisive factor in educational quality. The department aims to create motivation for teachers to work with dedication and peace of mind.

stories.title: TSC creates two new promotion pathways for teachers
stories.summary: The Teachers Service Commission has introduced a revised framework to address career stagnation among public school teachers. The new system creates two distinct paths: one for those remaining in classroom instruction and another for those pursuing school leadership. The review follows consultations with teachers' unions and stakeholders.

stories.title: TSC proposes major overhaul of teachers' promotion structure with two career paths
stories.summary: The Teachers Service Commission is proposing a new framework to separate classroom teaching from administrative leadership. The review of the 2018 Career Progression Guidelines aims to address concerns over career stagnation and unequal remuneration. The model seeks to provide promotion opportunities for teachers who prefer to remain in classrooms.

stories.title: Policymakers must give teachers a stronger voice on AI policy in schools
stories.summary: A new Cambridge University Press and Assessment report recommends that policymakers involve teachers in the design and procurement of AI tools. The report suggests that sustained professional learning is necessary to ensure educators can critically engage with technology. Policy should be grounded in the realities of the classroom.

stories.title: Florida city cancels St. Patrick’s Day event, citing DeSantis’s anti-DEI law - The Washington Post
Analysis: Why is Alberta ditching diversity, equity and inclusion in hiring practices?
stories.summary: The Alberta government is eliminating diversity, equity and inclusion from public sector hiring, citing a commitment to a merit-based system. Opposition members describe the move as political posturing. Experts and politics watchers remain divided on whether the change addresses a genuine problem or serves other interests.

stories.title: Jewish students hiding faith when applying to university, parents claim
stories.summary: A survey of Jewish parents found that some students are avoiding mentions of their faith or Hebrew language skills on university applications. Parents cited widespread concern regarding anti-Semitism on campuses. Some families are reportedly considering international options due to fears about the environment at domestic institutions.

stories.title: Lighthouse Learning expands Hyderabad footprint with strategic partnership with Meru International School
stories.summary: Lighthouse Learning has announced a partnership with Meru International School in Hyderabad. The collaboration combines Meru's inquiry-led philosophy with Lighthouse Learning's platform capabilities and academic expertise. The group aims to strengthen educational opportunities through this strategic integration of resources and networks.

stories.title: Haryana schools must act on gender-based bullying in 3 months: HC
stories.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has ordered all schools to ensure complaint systems cover bullying based on gender, identity, and sexual orientation. The state education department has three months to implement the directive. The court also instructed the CBSE to enforce its existing anti-bullying rules.

stories.title: Byron Donalds says teachers can't be replaced, defends school choice amid South Florida closures
stories.summary: Governor-elect Byron Donalds addressed concerns regarding AI in education during an event in South Florida. Emphasising that technology cannot replace human educators, he defended the role of teachers in the classroom. The event was hosted by LaunchEd to test and scale new educational technology products.

stories.title: Lighthouse Learning partners with Meru International School
stories.summary: Lighthouse Learning has partnered with Meru International School to strengthen academic delivery and faculty development. The collaboration combines Meru's inquiry-led approach with Lighthouse Learning's technology platforms and national network. The school currently operates two campuses in Hyderabad and is developing a third in Gopanpally.

stories.title: Lighthouse Learning acquires stake in Meru International School
stories.summary: Lighthouse Learning, a K-12 education company controlled by private equity firm KKR, has acquired a stake in Hyderabad-based Meru International School. The company described the move as a strategic partnership. Meru operates two campuses and offers both CBSE and Cambridge curricula from Early Years to Grade 12.

stories.title: Trump administration ends Head Start pay mandate
stories.summary: The Department of Health and Human Services has issued a final rule rolling back a Biden-era effort to increase salaries for Head Start staff. The previous policy aimed to keep wages competitive and reduce high turnover rates within the early education program.

stories.title: Frontier School Committee ends international trip sponsorship
stories.summary: The Frontier Regional School District will no longer sponsor international field trips under a new policy approved by the School Committee. While the committee acknowledged the educational value of travel, it voted to stop organizing or governing such excursions after the current academic year concludes.

stories.title: Bhiwandi municipal schools propose English-medium classes
stories.summary: The Bhiwandi Nizampur City Municipal Corporation has proposed introducing CBSE-affiliated English-medium classes to address declining enrollment. The initiative aims to provide affordable education to families who cannot pay private school fees. The proposal awaits approval from the municipal general body on November 17.

stories.title: Claremore Public Schools reaches $1M in teacher awards
stories.summary: Claremore Public Schools has distributed over $1 million in teacher awards through the Oklahoma Teacher Empowerment Program over the last three years. For the 2026-27 school year, the district recognized 32 educators with $372,000 in additional compensation. The recipients average 14.5 years of experience.

stories.title: CBSE introduces AI curriculum for Classes 3 to 8
stories.summary: The CBSE has launched a curriculum on computational thinking and artificial intelligence for students in Classes 3 to 8 for the 2026-27 session. The board plans to expand the program to Classes 9 and 10 next year. Educators are now debating how to teach technology alongside ethics.

stories.title: Guwahati student dies after incident at home
stories.summary: A Class 12 student in Guwahati allegedly stabbed his mother before jumping to his death from a high-rise building on Friday. The student sent messages to a school group prior to the incident, prompting the principal to notify police. The mother is currently recovering in a hospital.

stories.title: Delhi University adds students to safety committee
stories.summary: The University of Delhi has reconstituted its Committee on Women Safety and Security, including student representatives for the first time. The 13-member committee, headed by the university proctor, includes the DUSU president and secretary alongside various college principals and university officials.

stories.title: India shifts focus in school education policy
stories.summary: India's approach to school education has evolved from a focus on enrollment to foundational learning and holistic development. Recent shifts include the implementation of the National Education Policy 2020, expanded nutritional programs, and increased integration of technology and new teaching practices within the classroom.

stories.title: Schools report lack of resource persons
stories.summary: Despite the National Education Policy 2020 designating resource persons as the backbone of teacher support, many schools in Jammu and Kashmir report they have never seen one. Officials have suggested that selection should be handled by national-level researchers and monitored through technology to ensure accountability.

stories.title: Governor reviews Telangana university issues
stories.summary: Telangana Governor Shiv Pratap Shukla met with the Council of Higher Education chairman to review recent reports regarding state universities. The Governor requested a detailed report on academic and administrative activities and plans to convene a formal meeting with all university vice-chancellors to discuss institutional functioning.

stories.title: Jammu Sanskriti School hosts speedball championship
stories.summary: Jammu Sanskriti School in Kathua hosted the Open District-Level Speedball Championship 2026. The event, organized by the J&K Speed Ball Association, saw participation from approximately 250 students representing 10 schools across the district. Local police officials attended as guests.

stories.title: Kerala clears pending scholarship dues
stories.summary: The Kerala government has sanctioned 20.52 crore rupees to clear arrears for the CM Kids Scholarship scheme. The funds cover students who qualified in Lower and Upper Secondary Scholarship examinations. The government expects to disburse scholarship amounts for the current academic year by March 31.

stories.title: Calcutta High Court questions Abhishek Banerjee
stories.summary: The Calcutta High Court has questioned TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee regarding his claims that certain judges are loyal to the BJP. Banerjee made the allegations after the court declined an urgent hearing on his petition. The court has asked him to provide a list of the judges involved.

stories.title: Arunachal Pradesh to sponsor armed forces coaching
stories.summary: Arunachal Pradesh Chief Minister Pema Khandu announced a new government scheme to sponsor youth for coaching to join the armed forces. The state is collaborating with the Army to provide specialized training. The government also announced a phased infrastructure development plan for Dera Natung Government College.
